## Expected Behavior
Temporal should drop internode gRPC connections to pods that no longer exist after they are removed from the membership ring, avoiding repeated dial attempts to stale pod IPs.

## Actual Behavior
We are experiencing the same issue described in PR [https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/pull/8586](https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/pull/8586?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
Temporal servers keep stale internode gRPC connections after Kubernetes pods are terminated (during scale-down, rolling updates, or node drains). This results in continuous dial tcp … i/o timeout errors targeting IPs of pods that no longer exist.

## Steps to Reproduce the Problem

1. Deploy Temporal using the official Helm chart (services running as Deployments).
2. Trigger pod churn (e.g., rolling update, scaling down, or node drain).
3. Observe internode gRPC logs showing repeated dial attempts to the IPs of pods that have already been terminated.

## Specifications

  - Version: 1.25.2
  - Platform: Kubernetes, using the official Temporal Helm chart, Temporal services deployed as Deployments

## Additional Note / Question

Before a fix becomes available, is there any known workaround?

We are considering switching from Deployment to StatefulSet to have more stable pod identities, but this would require diverging from the official Helm chart, something we would prefer to avoid.

Any guidance would be greatly appreciated!

cc @prathyushpv if you can help take a look here.

Taking a look at the issue. I am working on a PR: https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/pull/9004
There is another component CachingRedirector which will hang on to history service connections for a few seconds even after that host has left the membership ring. I am trying to find an approach in which we don't close connections still used by CachingRedirector.

This is still happening. I noticed that the Temporal eventually recovers and remove the stale member. But it takes almost an hour and it generates thousands of noise in the logs. > Is there a workaround people are currently using to handle this issue?

set Guaranteed QoS on all the temporal services, give them a high PriorityClass, set PDBs + save-to-evict annotations false.

And then pray that one of the history or matching pods don't go down!!
Hello We see this issue happening on our cluster. Any fix planned yet?

Hello, sorry for the delay here. I am planning to fix this by merging these two PRs ASAP:
https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/pull/9277
https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/pull/10250

This should close and remove all references to stale connections.
